stem: Which room is preferred for a hospitalized client who requires Airborne Precautions?

options.A: An airborne infection isolation room with negative pressure relative to adjacent spaces.
options.B: A protective-environment room with positive pressure relative to adjacent spaces.
options.C: A semiprivate room with standard ventilation and the door left open.
options.D: A private room without controlled airflow or a defined pressure relationship.

rationale: CDC guidance states that the preferred placement for a patient requiring Airborne Precautions is an airborne infection isolation room (AIIR). An AIIR is maintained at negative pressure relative to surrounding areas so air flows into the room rather than outward. Therefore A is correct. A protective environment uses positive pressure for a different purpose, and ordinary private or semiprivate rooms without the AIIR airflow controls do not provide equivalent engineering protection when an AIIR is available.
educational_objective: Place hospitalized clients requiring Airborne Precautions in an AIIR with negative pressure relative to adjacent spaces when available.

correction_summary: Retained the original stem, options, and key A. Strengthened the final source to the CDC Airborne Precautions placement recommendation while retaining the glossary definition of negative pressure; no airflow-rate threshold was required or added to the item.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC isolation guidance; NCSBN 2026 for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC Airborne/Transmission-Based Precautions and glossary pages live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: Isolation Precautions > III.B.3 Airborne precautions; Transmission-Based Precautions > Use Airborne Precautions; Glossary > AIIR
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item tests only the preferred AIIR placement and negative-pressure direction; it does not require unsupported or unnecessary numeric ventilation parameters.

distractor_audit.A: Correct AIIR placement and pressure relationship.
distractor_audit.B: Positive pressure characterizes a Protective Environment and serves a different infection-control purpose.
distractor_audit.C: Standard semiprivate ventilation with an open door is not equivalent to an AIIR.
distractor_audit.D: A private room without controlled airflow is an interim fallback in limited-resource circumstances, not the preferred inpatient AIIR placement.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The stem asks for preferred placement; only A is the CDC-preferred AIIR configuration.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are room/airflow configurations with parallel structure.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — airborne transmission precautions and environmental controls.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC placement guidance, pressure definitions, each option, fallback-versus-preferred distinction, rationale, objective, NCSBN mapping, ambiguity and cueing. A remained uniquely correct.
